label: Early copy step (3rd output) of long sequences, token-modulated
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original tokens or <DEL>, and only when the input token has already appeared (in_first=0). It is concentrated on the first few copy steps of long sequences: recall_idx 1-3 holds 99% of activation mass and recall_idx 2 alone (input = orig(1), the step two after <DEL>) holds 73%. L=9 holds 84% of the mass, L=8 15%, and it is essentially silent for L<=6. Within that window it fires on only ~12-38% of steps, and which ones depends on the input token: with input in {3,c,m,o,e,v}, precision at recall_idx 2 with L=9 rises to 0.73, and other tokens (e.g. 0, l, p, s, y) often stay silent. The strongest activations are at recall_idx 2 with L=9 and one of these favoured tokens, with weaker spillover onto the neighbouring steps (recall_idx 1 and 3). The simple position predicate gets F1 ~0.43 on dev. The token dependence is graded and spread over many tokens, so no compact predicate captures it.
